analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 11.3.26
key_insights: Futures were mixed early (Nasdaq +30bps, S&P 500 and Russell 2000 -5bps) ahead of the US midterm elections. Prediction markets imply more than 90% odds Democrats win the House and more than 65% odds they win the Senate.

US/Iran are reviewing proposals from mediators. The US reportedly struck targets on Iran's Qeshm Island, which the NYT described as a small-scale defensive measure with no immediate plans to escalate. WTI rose 2% to $98.50 after falling 8% the prior day.

Tech earnings reactions in pre-market: AAPL -4% (gross margin and Services slowdown), DT -15% (F2Q ARR deceleration), SHOP -18% to -19% (in-line top line), PLTR -8% (decelerating sales growth outlook), ON +4% (upbeat sales forecast).
Disappointing software earnings combined with oversold semis appear to be driving semis over software early: SMH +2.5% vs IGV -1.5%.
GS Prime data: Global Fundamental L/S funds fell 3.49% in October (+9.1% YTD). TMT L/S funds lost 12.6% in October (+5.1% YTD). Global equities saw the largest net selling since March.

US Fundamental L/S gross leverage is at the 59th percentile over one year, while net leverage is at the 8th percentile. US Info Tech saw its largest notional net selling since June, driven by long sales. The Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.71, the 20th percentile over one year and the 7th over five years.

PLTR 3Q revenue was 7% above the Street with EBIT margin about 200bps above. Revenue growth accelerated to 96% from 93% in 2Q. FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to 5% above the Street and EBIT margin to about 150bps above. Forward indicators weakened: US Commercial TCV $1.5bn (+11% y/y vs +153% last quarter), RDV $6.5bn (+79% vs +124%), cRPO growth 88% vs 105%. Palantir attributed part of this to shorter contract durations with Sovereign AI customers.

AAPL F4Q26 EPS of $2.10 beat GS at $2.01 and consensus at $1.99. F1Q27 revenue guidance of 8-10% y/y growth beat consensus of about 6%. F1Q27 Services growth guidance of 8-9% missed, with App Store revenue flat y/y. Gross margin of 47.9% included a 100bps benefit from tariff refunds. F1Q27 gross margin guidance of 45-46% missed consensus of 46.9%, and GS sees cost headwinds, including memory, continuing beyond F1Q27.

ON 3Q revenue of $1.72bn was in line with GS and the Street ($1.71bn). EPS of $0.90 was in line with GS and above the Street at $0.88. AI Data Center revenue was disclosed for the first time at $180mn. The company expects $620mn of AI datacenter sales in 2026 vs $250mn in 2025. 4Q revenue guidance midpoint of $1.77bn is above the Street at $1.74bn. ON agreed to acquire Ferric for $600mn cash plus up to $175mn contingent consideration.

Other earnings first-takes: DOCN 3Q revenue accelerated to +40% y/y, FY26 revenue guide raised to about 34%, and CY27 growth guided to 60%+. DT F2Q ARR +16% y/y cc (down from +17%), subscription revenue +17% y/y cc, FY cc ARR guide raised by about 200bps, Investor Day February 16, 2027. SHOP GMV stable at about 30% y/y cc, revenue +32%, FCF margin 22%, 4Q revenue guided to low-30s y/y.

Bloomberg reports Disney is moving toward thousands of job cuts, with some managers asked to target 20% annual cost savings. Part of the savings would be reinvested in film, TV, technology, parks and cruise.

GS upgraded SIRI to Buy from Neutral and raised its price target to $37 from $33. The thesis includes a YouTube advertising partnership contributing about $1B of revenue and $125M of adjusted EBITDA by 2030E, and spectrum valued at $12 per share (up from $10). The stock is up about 40% YTD vs S&P 500 +10%.

Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal. Management cites a 2030 TAM rising from about $490bn to about $550bn, over $1bn of run-rate cost synergies, and non-GAAP EPS accretion within one year of close. GS does not rate Marvell.

GS hardware preview (DELL, HPE, NTAP, HPQ) for C3Q26: investors are split on whether enterprise IT spend is durable into 2027 or reflects memory cost inflation and demand pull-forward, with OEMs possibly over-earning on servers and storage. Investors are also concerned about the sustainability of neocloud demand and a possible shift to white-box procurement.
Street actions: upgrades NET (Overweight, JPMorgan), SIRI (Buy, Goldman Sachs), TWLO (Hold, HSBC). Downgrade MNDY (Hold, TD Cowen). Initiation DBX (Equal-Weight, Stephens).
Calendar: JOLTS and the midterm elections on Tue 11/3, US Services PMI and EU flash inflation on Wed 11/4, BoE rate decision on Thu 11/5, US NFP on Fri 11/6 (prior +29k).

Disappointing earnings (DT, SHOP, PLTR) led IGV down 1.5% pre-market.
Investors are split between a durable AI-driven enterprise IT refresh and memory-cost-driven over-earning with pull-forward risk.

earnings_insights: AAPL F4Q26 reported EPS $2.10 vs GS estimate $2.01 and consensus $1.99. Reported gross margin 47.9% vs GS 47.8% and consensus 46.9%, including a 100bps tariff refund benefit. F1Q27 guidance: revenue growth 8-10% y/y vs consensus about 6%, Services growth 8-9% (missed), gross margin 45-46% vs consensus 46.9%.

PLTR 3Q reported revenue 7% above the Street and EBIT margin about 200bps above. FY2026 revenue guidance raised to 5% above the Street. US Commercial TCV $1.5bn (+11% y/y vs +153% prior quarter), RDV $6.5bn (+79% vs +124%), cRPO growth 88% vs 105%.

ON 3Q reported revenue $1.72bn vs GS $1.72bn and Street (Visible Alpha) $1.71bn. Reported EPS $0.90 vs GS $0.90 and Street $0.88. Gross margin 41.2% vs 41.1%. Automotive $777mn (GS $820mn, Street $809mn), Industrial $467mn (GS $423mn, Street $426mn), Datacenter/Other $479mn (GS $477mn, Street $473mn). 4Q guidance: revenue midpoint $1.77bn (GS $1.79bn, Street $1.74bn), gross margin 42.5% (Street 42.1%), adjusted EPS $0.95-$1.07, midpoint $1.01 (GS $1.02, Street $0.95).
DOCN 3Q reported revenue growth +40% y/y, FY26 revenue growth guide raised to about 34%, CY27 guide of 60%+ y/y. Stock -1% pre-market.

DT F2Q reported ARR +16% y/y cc vs +17% in F1Q. Subscription revenue +17% y/y cc vs guidance of +15-16%. FY guidance raised for cc ARR by about 200bps and cc subscription revenue by about 125bps. Stock -15% pre-market.
SHOP reported GMV about +30% y/y cc, revenue +32% y/y cc, FCF margin 22%. 4Q guide: revenue growth low-30s y/y, gross profit growth high-20s y/y, flat FCF margin. Stock -18% to -19% pre-market.

Upcoming earnings: Tue 11/3 after close includes AMD, ANET, BKNG, TOST, XYZ, ALAB. Wed 11/4 includes UBER, DDOG, CRCL (pre) and APP, ARM, QCOM, SNAP, MELI, COHR (post). Thu 11/5 includes ABNB, AFRM, NET, MCHP, IONQ, LYFT, DKNG, AXON (post) and Sony, Nintendo (pre). Fri 11/6 includes CHTR, VST (pre).

tension_points.bull_case: Investors see a structural uplift in demand for compute, storage and networking tied to agentic AI and infrastructure refresh, a durable multi-year driver despite high ASPs.
tension_points.bear_case: Bearish investors attribute 2026 industry revenue strength to memory cost inflation and demand pull-forward, with OEMs over-earning on servers and storage and margins at risk if memory pricing slows or reverses.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown or reversal in memory pricing trends would pressure OEM margins, per the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: Constructive investors point to OEMs' design, supply-chain, integration and deployment capabilities versus ODM alternatives as a moat that justifies premium pricing.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors worry about the durability of neoclouds as customers and a shift to white-box procurement for compute, networking and storage.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Neoclouds moving to cloud-like white-box procurement models.
